{{Nihongo|'''Masaki Kashiwara'''|柏原 正樹|Kashiwara Masaki|born January 30, 1947|lead=yes}} is a Japanese mathematician and professor at the [[Kyoto University]] Institute for Advanced Study (KUIAS). He is known for his contributions to [[algebraic analysis]], [[microlocal analysis]], [[D-module|''D''-module]] theory, [[Hodge theory]], [[sheaf theory]] and [[representation theory]].<ref name="Pierre Schapira">{{cite arXiv|title= Masaki Kashiwara and Algebraic Analysis|author= Pierre Schapira |year= 2008 |class= math.HO |eprint=0810.4875}}</ref> He was awarded the [[Abel Prize]] in 2025,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Masaki Kashiwara |url=https://abelprize.no/abel-prize-laureates/2025 |access-date=March 26, 2025 |website=The Abel Prize}}</ref> and is the award's first recipient from Japan.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kyoto Univ. professor becomes 1st Japanese to win Abel Prize in math|url=https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2025/03/c29420c8260d-urgent-kyoto-univ-professor-becomes-1st-japanese-to-win-abel-prize-in-math.html |access-date=March 26, 2025 |website=Kyodo News |date=March 26, 2025 }}</ref>

==Biography==
Kashiwara was born in [[Yūki, Ibaraki]] on January 30, 1947.{{r|abelbio}}  One of his early mathematical fascinations was the [[wikt:鶴亀算|tsurukamezan]] problem, which asks the number of cranes and turtles given a set number of legs and heads.<ref name=":1" />

Kashiwara spent his undergraduate years at the [[University of Tokyo]] (UTokyo), earning his bachelor's degree in mathematics in 1969. He then went on to study at the same institution for his master's degree, which he completed in 1971.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.iwanami.co.jp/book/b265780.html |title=代数解析概論／柏原 正樹｜自然科学書 – 岩波書店 |language=ja}}</ref> At UTokyo, Kashiwara was a student of [[Mikio Sato]]. His master's thesis, written in Japanese, laid the foundations for the study of D-modules.<ref name="abelbio" /><ref name=":2" /> He continued studying under Sato at [[Kyoto University]] after Sato moved to the [[Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences]] (RIMS), earning his doctorate in 1974.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bischoff |first=Manon |title=Top Math Prize Recipient Wedded Algebra and Calculus to Found a New Field |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/top-math-prize-recipient-wedded-algebra-and-calculus-to-found-a-new-field/ |access-date=March 27, 2025 |website=Scientific American |language=en}}</ref>

He was a [[List of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|plenary speaker at International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1978 and an invited speaker in 1990.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers {{!}} International Mathematical Union (IMU) |url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=kashiwara&order=title&sort=desc |access-date=March 27, 2025 |website=www.mathunion.org}}</ref> He is a foreign associate of the [[French Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Masaki Kashiwara {{!}} Académie des sciences |url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/en/node/2265# |access-date=March 27, 2025 |website=www.academie-sciences.fr}}</ref> and a member of the [[Japan Academy]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Profile：Masaki Kashiwara |url=https://kuias.kyoto-u.ac.jp/e/profile/kashiwara |access-date=March 27, 2025 |website=KUIAS Kyoto University Institute for Advanced Study |language=en}}</ref> He has been involved in [[Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences]] (RIMS) since 1978 as a professor and later director.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Castelvecchi |first=Davide |date=March 26, 2025 |title=Mathematician who reshaped theory of symmetry wins Abel Prize |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-025-00949-9 |journal=Nature |volume=640 |issue=8057 |page=20 |language=en |doi=10.1038/d41586-025-00949-9 |pmid=40140514 |bibcode=2025Natur.640...20C |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":2" />

Kashiwara was awarded Japan's [[Order of the Sacred Treasure#2nd class, Gold and Silver Star|Order of the Sacred Treasure, Gold and Silver Star]] in 2020.<ref name=abelbio>{{cite web| title=Masaki Kashiwara: A brief biography|url=https://abelprize.no/biography/masaki-kashiwara-brief-biography|publisher=Abelprisen| access-date=March 27, 2025}}</ref>

He received the [[Abel Prize]] in 2025,<ref name=":0" /> the first Japanese national to do so.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Chang |first=Kenneth |date=March 26, 2025 |title=Masaki Kashiwara, Japanese Mathematician, Wins 2025 Abel Prize |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/03/26/science/abel-prize-math-masaki-kashiwara.html |access-date=March 27, 2025 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> The chairman of the Prize Committee, [[Helge Holden]], described Kashiwara's contributions as "very important in many different areas of mathematics,” and explained that Kashiwara "has solved some open conjectures — hard problems that have been around [and has] opened new avenues, connecting areas that were not known to be connected before.”<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 27, 2025 |title=Masaki Kashiwara wins Abel Prize for mathematicians |url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2025/03/27/japan/kashiwara-abel-prize/ |access-date=March 27, 2025 |website=The Japan Times |language=en}}</ref> The award ceremony is planned to be held at [[Oslo]], Norway on May 20, 2025.<ref name=":1" />

==Research==
Kashiwara and Sato established the foundations of the theory of [[systems of linear equations]] [[partial differential equations]] with [[analytic function]] coefficients, introducing the idea of applying [[sheaf cohomology]] to [[complex analysis]].<ref name="fifty-years"/> Kashiwara's master thesis states the foundations of [[D-module|''D''-module]] theory.<ref name="fifty-years">{{cite book |chapter=Fifty years of mathematics with Masaki Kashiwara |last=Schapira |first=Pierre |author-link=Pierre Schapira (mathematician) |chapter-url=https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~pierre.schapira/ConfSurveys/KICM1.pdf |title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians—Rio de Janeiro Plenary lectures |editor1-first=Boyan |editor1-last=Sirakov |editor2-first=Paulo Ney |editor2-last=de Souza |editor3-first=Marcelo |editor3-last=Viana |volume=1 |date=2018 |publisher=World Scientific Publishing |pages=97–110}}</ref> Kashiwara developed the analytic theory of ''D''-modules, while [[Joseph Bernstein]] introduced a similar approach in the algebraic case.<ref name="fifty-years"/>

Kashiwara's PhD thesis proves the rationality of the roots of b-functions ([[Bernstein–Sato polynomial]]s), using ''D''-module theory and [[resolution of singularities]].<ref name="Pierre Schapira" /><ref name="fifty-years"/>

Kashiwara's 1973 paper with Sato and [[Takahiro Kawai]] on the involutivity of characteristics of microdifferential systems and classification at generic points of microdifferential systems was described by [[Pierre Schapira (mathematician)|Pierre Schapira]] as having "an enormous influence on the analysis of partial differential equations".<ref name="fifty-years"/>

==Books==
*''Seminar on Micro-Local Analysis'', by [[Victor Guillemin]], Masaki Kashiwara, and Takahiro Kawai (1979), {{ISBN|978-0-691-08232-5}}
*''Systems of Microdifferential Equations'', by Masaki Kashiwara; notes and translation by Teresa Monteiro Fernandes; introduction by [[Jean-Luc Brylinski]] (1983), {{ISBN|978-0-8176-3138-3}}
*''Introduction to Microlocal Analysis'', by Masaki Kashiwara (1986)
*''Foundations of Algebraic Analysis'', by Masaki Kashiwara, [[Takahiro Kawai]], and Tatsuo Kimura; translated by Goro Kato (1986), {{ISBN|978-0-691-08413-8}}
*''Algebraic Analysis : Papers Dedicated to Professor Mikio Sato on the Occasion of His Sixtieth Birthday'', edited by Masaki Kashiwara, [[Takahiro Kawai]] (1988), {{ISBN|978-0-12-400466-5}}
*''Sheaves on Manifolds'' : With a Short History <Les débuts de la théorie des faisceaux> by Christian Houzel, by Masaki Kashiwara, [[Pierre Schapira (mathematician)|Pierre Schapira]] (1990), {{ISBN|978-3-540-51861-7}}
*''Topological Field Theory, Primitive Forms and Related Topics'', by Masaki Kashiwara ''et al.''(1998), {{ISBN|978-0-8176-3975-4}}
*''Physical Combinatorics'', Masaki Kashiwara, [[Tetsuji Miwa]], editors (2000), {{ISBN|978-1-4612-7121-5}}
*''MathPhys Odyssey 2001: Integrable Models and Beyond: In Honor of Barry M. McCoy'', Masaki Kashiwara and [[Tetsuji Miwa]], editors (2002), {{ISBN|978-0-8176-4260-0}}
*''Bases cristallines des groupes quantiques'', by Masaki Kashiwara (rédigé par Charles Cochet); Cours Spécialisés 9 (2002), viii+115 pages, {{ISBN|978-2-85629-126-9}}
*''D-Modules and Microlocal Calculus'', Masaki Kashiwara; translated by Mutsumi Saito (2003), {{ISBN|978-0-8218-2766-6}}
*''Categories and Sheaves'', Masaki Kashiwara and Pierre Schapira (2006), {{ISBN|978-3-540-27949-5}}
